title: Starter Kits — field notes & blockers (Aug 04 2026)
content:
Context: quick sync after the cross-functional kit playtest last week. Goal: turn the ‘starter kits’ experiment into a predictable onramp path for new engineers and trial users (web, python, node, docker). Notes below are raw — working doc for the kit owners and anyone iterating on quickstarts/samples.

What we tried this week
- Field test: 12 external devs followed the python + docker kit. Most finished within 22–35 minutes, median ~28m.
- Added a tiny sandbox model (gptx-mini) to lower run cost during onboarding. Worked for 9/12; 3 reported token limit surprise when running long prompts.
- New template selector in the web quickstart (PR #621) improved discoverability but caused a visual shift in dark mode — CSS variables mismatch across docs theme.

Observed friction / blockers
- Pip packaging step in the python quickstart flakes on mac-latest CI: intermittent timeout when pip-installing wheel from artifacts (suspect network throttling).
- OIDC examples for Private deployment are outdated: audience claim and redirect URI examples fail against our test VPC (INF-4823).
- Telemetry naming inconsistent: sample events use mixed namespaces (sample.start vs starter.kit.start) — makes analytics queries noisy.
- Docs deep-links: anchor IDs generated from slide titles sometimes duplicate (slides -> headings) causing jump-to-anchor to pick the wrong section.

Unresolved questions
- Do we keep the sandbox model in the published quickstart or make it opt-in via a toggle? (cost vs easiest success)
- Who approves security copy for the Docker image tags? Need a quick path for publishing dev-friendly images without full SOC review.

Immediate next actions (owners)
- Alex Chen: retry CI with artifact host change, escalate flaky pip step, ETA: 2026-08-06.
- Priya Malhotra: open quick PR with telemetry namespace normalization, add test case for event schema, ETA: 2026-08-07.
- Maya Singh: draft proposal to make sandbox toggled by default in the hosted quickstart (pros/cons + cost estimates), link to INF-4823, ETA: 2026-08-09.
- Diego Ramirez: dark mode CSS fix for template selector, verify across docs themes, ETA: 2026-08-05.

Quick wins to push this sprint
- Add a one-line note at top of python quickstart about long-prompt token behavior (owner: Maya) — <30m change.
- Add a smoke e2e step for OIDC sample in the private-dev pipeline (owner: Diego) — helps catch INF-4823 regressions.

Risks to call out
- If we ship the sandbox-on-by-default, cost could increase ~8–12% for new signups in first 30 days (estimate, based on last experiment). Need finance sign-off for credits budget.
- CI flakes slow down PR cadence; consider temporary windows for longer timeouts for onboarding kit publishes.

Meeting follow-up / decisions needed by next sync
- Decision: sandbox toggle default? (prod cost vs reduced support overhead)
- Approval: temporary Docker image publish checklist for dev images

Slack threads & PRs referenced
- slack: #dx-starter-kits thread: "field test learnings" (link in Confluence page)
- github: PR #621 (template selector), PR #626 (docker image labels)

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Consider an ‘onboarding checklist’ endpoint that returns a tiny JSON of remaining steps to finish the kit (helps embedders show progress).
- Could pair the telemetry normalization with a small dashboard in the console showing conversion from kit start -> finished -> api calls made in first 24h.

If you want to take an action above, add a comment below, tag owner, and we’ll triage in the Friday DX sync.
